**Answer: $d(n,q)=q^{\,n-2}\,d(2,q)$**

I did not fully derive the lower bound. The upper bound below is verified, and the equality is the value I believe the known result gives.

**Upper bound via projection.** Take a codeword $c_\pi$ of weight $d(2,q)$ in $\mathcal C_1(2,q)^\perp$ on a plane $\pi\subseteq\mathrm{PG}(n,q)$. Fix a subspace $S$ of projective dimension $n-3$ disjoint from $\pi$, and project from $S$ onto $\pi$. Define $c(P)=c_\pi(\bar P)$ for $P\notin S$ and $c(P)=0$ for $P\in S$, where $\bar P$ is the image of $P$.

- A line disjoint from $S$ that projects onto a line of $\pi$ has sum $\sum_{x\in\text{line}} c_\pi(x)\equiv 0 \pmod p$.
- A line that projects to a single point $x$ has sum $q\,c_\pi(x)\equiv 0 \pmod p$, since $q$ is a power of $p$.

So $c$ lies in the kernel. Each point of $\pi$ has exactly $q^{n-2}$ preimages outside $S$, so $\mathrm{wt}(c)=q^{n-2}\,d(2,q)$. Hence $d(n,q)\le q^{n-2}d(2,q)$.

**Consistency check.** For $n>2$, the hyperplane difference $\chi_{H_1}-\chi_{H_2}$ is also a codeword, with weight $2q^{n-1}$. Since $d(2,q)\le 2q$ (from the analogous construction in a plane), this is never smaller than $q^{n-2}d(2,q)$.

ANSWER: $d(n,q)=q^{\,n-2}\,d(2,q)$
